answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may trade, then slash that stake when a blinded audit finds fabricated deliveries or collusive claims. A single attacker can still create many identities, but must fund every one and risks losing the capital; splitting activity across names no longer makes fraud free. For example, an umber-market dawn audit might expose an ember shipment claimed by several linked agents. The stake raises the cost of scaling Sybils rather than proving that identities are unique.
